steps.title: Import Angular core modules and create AuthService
steps.instruction: Import Component, Injectable, and Input from '@angular/core'. Then create an AuthService class with a simple isAuthenticated property set to false.
steps.hint: Use the @Injectable() decorator to make the service injectable. Define isAuthenticated as a public boolean property.
steps.seedCode: // Import Angular core modules and create AuthService
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have imported the necessary Angular modules and created a basic authentication service with an isAuthenticated property.
successCriteria: Component, Injectable, and Input are imported from '@angular/core'. An AuthService class is created with @Injectable() decorator and has a public isAuthenticated property initialized to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the Angular core modules and created the AuthService with the required property.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've imported all three symbols (Component, Injectable, Input) and created the AuthService class with the isAuthenticated property.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import Component, Injectable, and Input from '@angular/core', then create an AuthService class with a public isAuthenticated property set to false.

steps.title: Create a base component to be wrapped
steps.instruction: Create a UserProfileComponent class that displays a welcome message. This component will later be wrapped with authentication.
steps.hint: Define a new component class with a template that shows a simple welcome message.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Angular core modules and create AuthService


// Create UserProfileComponent here
steps.expectedOutcome: A UserProfileComponent class is created with a template showing a welcome message.
successCriteria: UserProfileComponent is defined as a class with @Component decorator and a template containing a welcome message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the base UserProfileComponent that will be enhanced with authentication.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your component has both the @Component decorator and a template with a welcome message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't properly defined. Check that you've created a class with @Component decorator and a template.

steps.title: Define the HOC function structure
steps.instruction: Create a function called withAuth that takes a component class as a parameter and returns a new component class. Place it after the UserProfileComponent.
steps.hint: In Angular, a HOC is typically a function that wraps a component. Start with: export function withAuth(Component: any) { return class extends Component {} }
steps.expectedOutcome: A withAuth function is defined that accepts a component and returns a new component class.
successCriteria: The withAuth function is created with the correct signature and returns a class that extends the input component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the basic structure of the withAuth HOC function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your withAuth function takes a component parameter and returns a class that extends it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The withAuth function structure isn't quite right. It should accept a component and return a new component class.

steps.title: Add Component decorator to the HOC
steps.instruction: Add the @Component decorator to the class returned by the withAuth function. Set the selector to 'app-auth-wrapper' and the template to '<ng-content></ng-content>'.
steps.hint: Remember to import Component from '@angular/core' if not already imported. The decorator should be placed directly above the class definition.
steps.expectedOutcome: The HOC class now has Angular metadata, making it a proper Angular component that can project content.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator is added to the AuthWrapper class with selector 'app-auth-wrapper' and template '<ng-content></ng-content>'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the Component decorator to the HOC. This makes it a valid Angular component that can be used in templates.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the decorator, but check the selector and template values. They should be exactly 'app-auth-wrapper' and '<ng-content></ng-content>'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HOC class still needs the @Component decorator with proper metadata. Review Angular component basics.

steps.title: Inject AuthService into the HOC
steps.instruction: Add a constructor to the AuthWrapper class that injects AuthService and stores it as a property.
steps.hint: Use Angular's dependency injection in the constructor to receive an AuthService instance and assign it to a class property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The HOC class now has a constructor that properly injects AuthService and stores it for later use.
successCriteria: AuthWrapper class has a constructor that injects AuthService and assigns it to a class property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully injected AuthService into the HOC using Angular's dependency injection.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the constructor properly receives AuthService and assigns it to a class property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The constructor should inject AuthService and store it as a property. Check the syntax for Angular dependency injection.

steps.title: Implement authentication check logic
steps.instruction: In the AuthWrapper class, add a property called 'isAuthenticated' that gets its value from the injected AuthService's isAuthenticated property.
steps.hint: You can assign the AuthService's isAuthenticated property to a class property in the constructor.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthWrapper class will have an isAuthenticated property that reflects the authentication state from AuthService.
successCriteria: AuthWrapper class has an isAuthenticated property that is assigned from AuthService.isAuthenticated in the constructor.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the authentication state to your HOC wrapper.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're assigning the AuthService's isAuthenticated property to a class property called 'isAuthenticated'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The authentication check logic isn't implemented correctly. You need to add an isAuthenticated property to AuthWrapper that gets its value from the injected AuthService.

steps.title: Render the wrapped component when authenticated
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthWrapper class, add a template that conditionally renders the WrappedComponent when isAuthenticated is true.
steps.hint: Use Angular's template syntax with *ngIf to conditionally render the wrapped component. You'll need to access the WrappedComponent parameter from the withAuth function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthWrapper class now has a template that will display the wrapped component only when the user is authenticated.
successCriteria: The AuthWrapper class includes a template with *ngIf that conditionally renders the WrappedComponent based on isAuthenticated.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional rendering to display the wrapped component when authenticated.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your template includes *ngIf to conditionally render the WrappedComponent based on isAuthenticated.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should use *ngIf to conditionally render the WrappedComponent when isAuthenticated is true. Check Angular's template syntax.

steps.title: Pass inputs to the wrapped component
steps.instruction: Define an @Input() property named 'username' in the AuthWrapper class to receive data from the parent component.
steps.hint: Add the @Input() decorator above a property declaration in the class. This will allow the HOC to receive data from outside.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthWrapper class will have an @Input() property that can receive data from parent components.
successCriteria: The AuthWrapper class contains an @Input() property named 'username'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added an @Input() property to the HOC. This allows the wrapper to receive data from parent components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the @Input() decorator and named the property 'username'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AuthWrapper class doesn't have an @Input() property named 'username'. Remember to use the @Input() decorator.

steps.title: Use the HOC to wrap the base component
steps.instruction: Create a constant named 'WrappedUserProfile' that calls the 'withAuth' function with 'UserProfileComponent' as its argument, then export this wrapped component.
steps.hint: Use the 'withAuth' HOC function you defined earlier to wrap the base component. Assign the result to a constant and export it.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a new constant 'WrappedUserProfile' that holds the result of calling 'withAuth' with 'UserProfileComponent', and this wrapped component will be exported.
successCriteria: The constant 'WrappedUserProfile' is created, calls 'withAuth(UserProfileComponent)', and is exported.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created and exported the wrapped component using the HOC.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the constant, but make sure it calls 'withAuth' with 'UserProfileComponent' and is exported.
steps.feedbackWrong: The wrapped component was not created or exported correctly. Review the HOC usage syntax.

steps.title: Provide and use the AuthService
steps.instruction: Add AuthService to the providers array of the AppModule to make it available for dependency injection throughout the application.
steps.hint: In Angular, services must be provided at a module or component level. Add AuthService to the providers array in the @NgModule decorator of AppModule.
steps.expectedOutcome: AuthService will be available for dependency injection in the HOC and other components.
successCriteria: AuthService is added to the providers array of AppModule.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! AuthService is now properly provided and can be injected into the HOC.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a provider, but make sure it's specifically AuthService in the AppModule providers array.
steps.feedbackWrong: AuthService needs to be provided at the module level. Add it to the providers array in AppModule.

steps.title: Use the wrapped component in a template
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent template, add the selector for the wrapped component (e.g., <app-user-profile>) and bind a sample input value to it using property binding.
steps.hint: Use the component selector you defined in the wrapped component's @Component decorator. Bind an input property using [propertyName]="value" syntax.
steps.analogousExample:
// Using a component with input binding in a template
<app-greeting [name]="'Alice'"></app-greeting>
steps.expectedOutcome: The wrapped component will be rendered in the AppComponent template with a bound input value when the application runs.
successCriteria: The AppComponent template contains the wrapped component's selector with property binding for an input value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully integrated the HOC-wrapped component into the template with input binding.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the component selector, but make sure to include property binding for an input value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The wrapped component is not properly added to the template. Check the selector and input binding syntax.

steps.title: Test the authentication flow
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent template, add a button that toggles the authentication state by calling a method on the AuthService, then observe how the HOC conditionally renders the wrapped component.
steps.hint: Inject AuthService into AppComponent, create a method that toggles its authentication state, and add a button in the template that calls this method.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent will have a button that toggles authentication state, allowing you to verify the HOC's conditional rendering behavior.
successCriteria: AppComponent injects AuthService, has a toggleAuth method, and the template includes a button that calls toggleAuth() to change authentication state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented authentication state toggling. Click the button to see the HOC conditionally render the wrapped component based on the authentication state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've injected AuthService into AppComponent, created a toggleAuth method, and added a button in the template that calls this method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The authentication toggle functionality isn't complete. Review how to inject services in Angular components and add click handlers to buttons.
